title: Lioaryn as çhengey
description: Ten short stories about books and language: a new Manx dictionary and its sounds, a weekly book review of a novel about solitude, an old Manx catechism found in a church chest, a picture book about a sparrow, a science textbook translated into Manx, a history of Douglas harbour, a cookbook of old recipes, a fire at a second-hand bookshop, a Christmas television programme in Manx, and a climber's guidebook to a hill path.

lessons.title: Yn fockleyr noa
lessons.summary: Glenys Tregoning is writing a new Manx dictionary in Douglas, and the linguistics student Emyr helps her for a summer; she explains why Manx spelling is misleading for learners and why each entry needs an accurate note on how to say the word, shows him a back vowel and the voicing he can feel in his throat, talks about whether the power to learn a language is innate, and adds greetings and a wise old saying to the dictionary.
lessons.text:
Ta Glenys Tregoning gobbraghey er fockleyr noa Gaelg as Baarle ayns Doolish. Ta'n obbyr mooar, as bee eh bleeantyn roish my vees y fockleyr aarloo. Dagh moghrey, t'ee goaill fockle noa. T'ee screeu yn keeal echey ayns Baarle, sampleyr jeh'n fockle ayns raa, as yn aght dy ghra eh.

'Sy tourey shoh, ta studeyr aeg gobbraghey marish: Emyr, ta jannoo studeyrys er çhengoaylleeaght ec yn ollooscoill. Un laa, dooyrt Emyr: “Cre'n fa ta shiu screeu yn aght dy ghra dagh fockle? Ta'n fockle screeuit ayns shen hannah.”

“Er-y-fa dy vel y screeu Gaelg meestiuragh,” dooyrt Glenys. “Ta'n lettraghey Gaelg çheet er lettraghey ny Baarle. My ta peiagh lhaih fockle Gaelg myr fockle Baarle, cha jean eh gra eh dy kiart. Ta'n screeu meestiuragh son sleih noa, as er-y-fa shen lhisagh shin cur fys feerysagh daue mychione ny sheeanyn.”

Ren ee soilshaghey sampleyr da. “Jeeagh er y fockle shoh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n sheean 'sy vean cooyllagh: t'eh çheet veih cooyllagh y veeal, as cha nel eh çheet veih'n toshiaght. Ta sleih ta gynsaghey Gaelg jannoo y sheean shoh ec toshiaght y veeal, as cha nel shen kiart. Lhisagh shin screeu dy feerysagh dy vel y sheean cooyllagh.”

Eisht loayr ee mychione y cronnane. “Ta cronnane ayns corocklyn ennagh,” dooyrt ee. “Cur dty laue er dty scoarnagh, as abbyr ‘v’ as eisht ‘f’. Lesh ‘v’, ta cronnane ayn, as t'ou goaill baght jeh craa fo dty laue. Lesh ‘f’, cha nel cronnane erbee.” Ren Emyr shen, as va craa fo e laue.

“Kys ta lhiannoo gynsaghey ny sheeanyn shoh ooilley?” dooyrt Emyr. “Cha nel fys mie ec peiagh erbee,” dooyrt Glenys. “Ta çhengoaylleeyn ennagh gra dy vel y phooar dy ynsagh çhengey coruggyragh: t'ee ayns dy chooilley lhiannoo veih'n laa t'eh ruggit. Cha nel ad ooilley coardail rish shen. Vel y phooar coruggyragh, ny vel ee çheet lesh cliaghtey? She feysht vooar ee.”

Ta ram bannaghtyn ayns y fockleyr neesht: ny bannaghtyn ta sleih gra dagh laa, myr moghrey mie, fastyr mie as oie vie. Ta bannaght ayns raaghyn shenn neesht, myr “Bannaght Yee ort”.

Cha nel dagh fockle cooie son y fockleyr. Roish my vel Glenys screeu fockle noa, t'ee briaght jee hene mychione cooieid y fockle: vel sleih jannoo ymmyd jeh? Tra nagh vel cooieid echey, cha nel ee screeu eh.

Ec jerrey y tourey, hug Glenys raa creeney 'sy fockleyr: “Gyn çhengey, gyn çheer.” “She raa creeney eh,” dooyrt Emyr.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Glenys jannoo ayns Doolish?
T'ee gobbraghey er fockleyr noa Gaelg as Baarle.
Cre'n fa ta Glenys screeu yn aght dy ghra dagh fockle?
Er-y-fa dy vel y screeu Gaelg meestiuragh son sleih noa.
Cre lhisagh fockleyr cur da sleih noa mychione ny sheeanyn?
Lhisagh eh cur fys feerysagh daue.
Cre hooar Emyr fo e laue lesh ‘v’?
Hooar eh craa, er-y-fa dy vel cronnane ayns ‘v’.
Vel dy chooilley çhengoayllee coardail dy vel y phooar dy ynsagh çhengey coruggyragh?
Cha nel. Cha nel ad ooilley coardail rish shen.
Cre'n raa creeney hug Glenys 'sy fockleyr?
Hug ee “Gyn çhengey, gyn çheer” 'sy fockleyr.

lessons.title: Y baghteyrys 'sy phabyr shiaghtinoil
lessons.summary: Mererid Tonkin writes book reviews for a weekly paper in Douglas and for a literary journal; she reads the new novel by Islwyn Retallack, whose first book ten years ago was a failure that gave him a bad name, finds that this story of an old fisherman's solitude, his memories and his friendship with a young woman gives her great pleasure, praises it in her review, and gets a grateful letter from him.
lessons.text:
Ta Mererid Tonkin screeu baghteyrys lioaryn son pabyr naight shiaghtinoil ayns Doolish. Dagh Jeheiney, ta'n pabyr shiaghtinoil çheet magh, as ta baghteyrys noa eck ayn. Dagh shiaghtin, t'ee lhaih lioar noa, as t'ee screeu mychione: vel y lioar mie, ny vel ee olk, as cre'n fa? Ta Mererid screeu son jurnyl neesht: jurnyl mychione lettyraght, ta çheet magh keayrt 'sy vlein.

'Sy vee shoh, hooar Mererid lioar noa veih Islwyn Retallack. Va lioar elley screeuit ec Islwyn roish jeih bleeaney, agh va'n lioar shen ny failleilys. Cha row sleih kionnaghey ee, as dooyrt ny cremeyderyn dy row ee feer olk. Va anghoo er Islwyn ec y traa shen: dooyrt sleih nagh row eh ny screeudeyr mie. Lurg y failleilys shen, cha screeu eh lioar erbee rish jeih bleeaney.

Ta'n lioar noa mychione shenn eeasteyr ta cummal ny lomarcan er ellan veg. Ta'n lioar loayrt mychione y lomarcanys echey: cha nel peiagh erbee elley er yn ellan, as cha nel eh loayrt rish peiagh erbee rish shiaghtinyn. Ayns y lomarcanys shen, t'eh smooinaghtyn er e vea. Ta'n lioar lane dy aachooinaghtyn: aachooinaghtyn er e ayr as e voir, er e ven, as er ny laghyn v'eh aeg ayns Rhumsaa.

Eisht ta ben aeg çheet dys yn ellan, as t'ee jannoo studeyrys er ny ushagyn. Ta ainjys çheet eddyr y shenn dooinney as y ven aeg. Cha nel y lioar mychione graih: t'ee mychione ainjys veg eddyr daa pheiagh. Ta'n shenn eeasteyr gynsaghey dy loayrt reesht, as ta'n lomarcanys echey goll ersooyl beggan as beggan.

Ren Mererid lhaih y lioar ayns daa laa. Va eunys mooar eck ayns y lioar. Ayns e baghteyrys 'sy phabyr shiaghtinoil, screeu ee: “Hug y lioar shoh eunys orrym nagh row aym rish bleeantyn. Ta'n screeu feer aalin, as ta'n shenn eeasteyr cho bio as peiagh ayns my hie hene.” Screeu ee neesht dy row anghoo er Islwyn kyndagh rish y chied lioar, agh nagh lhisagh anghoo erbee ve er nish.

Lurg shiaghtin, haink lettyr veih Islwyn. “Gura mie ayd son y baghteyrys,” screeu eh. “Lurg y failleilys, va mee ayns lomarcanys myr yn eeasteyr 'sy lioar. Ta ny aachooinaghtyn echey cosoylagh rish my aachooinaghtyn hene. Hug dty ockle eunys orrym.”

'Sy gheurey, screeu Mererid baghteyrys liauyr son y jurnyl. Ayns y jurnyl, screeu ee mychione ainjys as lomarcanys ayns lioaryn Islwyn.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Mererid screeu son y pabyr shiaghtinoil?
T'ee screeu baghteyrys lioaryn son y pabyr shiaghtinoil.
Cre haghyr da'n chied lioar ec Islwyn?
Va'n chied lioar ny failleilys, as va anghoo er Islwyn ec y traa shen.
Quoi ta cummal er yn ellan veg 'sy lioar noa?
Ta shenn eeasteyr cummal ny lomarcan er yn ellan.
Cre ta çheet eddyr y shenn dooinney as y ven aeg?
Ta ainjys çheet eddyr y shenn dooinney as y ven aeg.
Cre screeu Mererid son y jurnyl?
Screeu ee baghteyrys liauyr mychione ainjys as lomarcanys ayns lioaryn Islwyn.

lessons.title: Y catechism ayns y kishtey
lessons.summary: The vicar Geraint Prosser finds a small old book in a chest in his church in the north of the island; the scholar Aisling Moran sees that it is a copy of the Manx catechism printed in 1707, explains its questions on conscience and the canonical books, reads the name of the rich woman who paid for the copies, links a royalist priest of the Civil War to the church, and the book is shown to the parish at a small ceremony that begins with a little bell.
lessons.text:
She saggyrt Geraint Prosser ayns keeill veg shenn 'sy twoaie jeh'n ellan. Un laa 'sy gheurey, v'eh glenney kishtey shenn 'sy cheeill, as hooar eh lioar veg ayns y kishtey. Va'n coodagh doo as shenn, as va ny duillagyn buigh. Va'n lioar ayns Gaelg: she catechism v'ayn, lioar veg lesh feyshtyn as freggyrtyn mychione y chredjue.

Va enney ec Geraint er scruteyder: Aisling Moran, ta jannoo studeyrys er shenn lioaryn Gaelg ec yn ollooscoill. Haink y scruteyder dys y cheeill er y nah laa. Ren ee jeeaghyn er y catechism rish tammylt liauyr. “She coip jeh'n chied lioar phrentit ayns Gaelg,” dooyrt ee. “Va'n catechism shoh prentit 'sy vlein 1707. Cha nel agh kuse dy choipyn foast er mayrn.”

Ren y scruteyder lhaih kuse dy ghuillagyn da Geraint. “Ta feysht ayn mychione y cooinsheanse,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n freggyrt gra dy vel y cooinsheanse myr coraa ayns cree dy chooilley pheiagh, as t'eh gra rish y pheiagh cre ta kiart as cre ta olk. Ta feyshtyn ayn mychione ny lioaryn canoanagh y Vible neesht: ny lioaryn ta'n agglish goaill myr lioaryn canoanagh, as cre'n fa nagh vel lioaryn elley canoanagh.”

Er y chied duillag, va ennym screeuit lesh laue: ennym y phatroon. “Va'n patroon ny ben verçhagh,” dooyrt Aisling. “Ren ee eeck son ny coipyn, as hug ee ad da paitçhyn y skeerey. Er-y-fa shen, va'n catechism ec dy chooilley lught-thie 'sy skeerey.”

Ta clagh veg er voalley y cheeill son saggyrt va 'sy cheeill 'sy Chaggey Theayagh. “V'eh reeoilagh,” dooyrt Geraint. “V'eh lesh y ree.” “Va ram jeh'n clere reeoilagh ec y traa shen,” dooyrt yn scruteyder. “Cha row eh aashagh son y clere tra va'n caggey er jerrey.”

Lurg shen, va'n catechism soit ayns kishtey gless 'sy cheeill, as ren y clere sharmanys beg. Haink yn aspick dys y sharmanys, as haink sleih y skeerey. Ec toshiaght y sharmanys, ren paitçhey aeg bwoalley clageen beg. Va sheean y clageen feer veen 'sy cheeill. Eisht ren yn aspick lhaih feysht as freggyrt veih'n catechism ayns Gaelg. Ec jerrey y sharmanys, ren y paitçhey bwoalley y clageen reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre hooar Geraint 'sy kishtey?
Hooar eh lioar veg: she catechism v'ayn ayns Gaelg.
Quoi ta Aisling Moran?
She scruteyder ee, ta jannoo studeyrys er shenn lioaryn Gaelg.
Cre ta'n catechism gra mychione y cooinsheanse?
T'eh gra dy vel y cooinsheanse myr coraa ayns cree dy chooilley pheiagh.
Cre ren y patroon?
Ren ee eeck son ny coipyn, as hug ee ad da paitçhyn y skeerey.
Quoi va reeoilagh 'sy Chaggey Theayagh?
Va'n saggyrt va 'sy cheeill 'sy Chaggey Theayagh reeoilagh.
Cre ren y paitçhey aeg ec toshiaght y sharmanys?
Ren eh bwoalley clageen beg.

lessons.title: Lioar y sparroo
lessons.summary: Heulwen Laity writes and draws picture books for small children, and her six-year-old grandson Caradog listens to each new page of her book about a sparrow: a flowering tree with a sweet scent, the insects the sparrow feeds its chicks in summer, a cat with soft paws and sharp claws, an old dog with bristly hair, and wavy fields; when he sees the pictures he calls her a magician.
lessons.text:
Ta Heulwen Laity screeu lioaryn son paitçhyn beggey. T'ee screeu ny skeealyn, as t'ee tayrn ny jallooyn hene. 'Sy tourey shoh, t'ee screeu lioar noa mychione sparroo. Ta'n sparroo cummal ayns garey ec shenn thie faggys da balley beg.

Ta mac e inneen, Caradog, shey bleeaney d'eash, cummal marish e shenn-voir 'sy tourey. Dagh moghrey, ta Heulwen lhaih duillag noa da Caradog, as t'eh gra dy vel y skeeal mie, ny nagh vel.

Ayns y chied jalloo, ta'n sparroo ayns billey blaaoil. Ta'n billey blaaoil lane dy vlaaghyn baney, as ta cooraght villish ayns yn aer. “Cre ta cooraght?” dooyrt Caradog. “She soar mie eh,” dooyrt Heulwen. “Ta cooraght ec ny blaaghyn.” Hie Caradog magh dys y garey, as ren eh soar ny blaaghyn er y billey blaaoil ayns shen. “Ta cooraght villish oc!” dooyrt eh.

Ayns y nah jalloo, ta'n sparroo shirrey bee. 'Sy tourey, ta'n sparroo beishteigagh: t'eh gee beishteigyn beggey veih ny duillagyn. “Nagh vel y sparroo gee rassyn?” dooyrt Caradog. “T'eh gee rassyn neesht,” dooyrt Heulwen, “agh 'sy tourey t'eh cur beishteigyn da ny ein echey. Ta ny ein beishteigagh.”

Eisht ta kayt çheet dys y garey. Ta maaigyn bog ec y chayt, as ta buiggys ayns e fynney. Agh ta ingnyn geyre ayns ny maaigyn echey. Ta'n sparroo goll seose 'sy billey, as cha nod y kayt geddyn eh. “Ta buiggys ayns maaigyn y chayt,” dooyrt Caradog, “agh cha nel ny maaigyn mie son ushag.”

Ayns y jalloo shen, ta shenn voddey çheet neesht, as ta fynney caulgagh echey. Ta'n moddey roie lurg y chayt, as ta'n kayt roie ersooyl. “Ta fynney caulgagh ec y moddey ain neesht!” dooyrt Caradog. “T'eh caulgagh myr y moddey shoh 'sy lioar.”

Ayns y jalloo s'jerree, ta'n sparroo etlagh harrish ny magheryn. Ta ny magheryn tonnagh, myr y keayn, as ta'n faiyr tonnagh 'sy gheay. Va Caradog jeeaghyn er y jalloo rish tammylt liauyr.

Tra honnick eh ny jallooyn ooilley, dooyrt eh: “T'ou myr druaightagh, Shenn-voir! Ta'n sparroo shoh bio!” Va Heulwen gearey. “Cha nel mee my druaightagh,” dooyrt ee. “Agh ta druaightagh beg ayns dy chooilley lioar vie.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Heulwen screeu 'sy tourey shoh?
T'ee screeu lioar noa mychione sparroo.
Cre t'ayns yn aer mygeayrt y billey blaaoil?
Ta cooraght villish ayns yn aer.
Cre ta'n sparroo gee 'sy tourey?
'Sy tourey, ta'n sparroo beishteigagh: t'eh gee beishteigyn beggey.
Cre t'ec y chayt?
Ta maaigyn bog ec y chayt, as ta buiggys ayns e fynney.
Kys ta ny magheryn ayns y jalloo s'jerree?
Ta ny magheryn tonnagh, myr y keayn.
Cre t'ec y shenn voddey?
Ta fynney caulgagh ec y shenn voddey.
Cre dooyrt Caradog tra honnick eh ny jallooyn ooilley?
Dooyrt eh dy row e shenn-voir myr druaightagh.

lessons.title: Y lioar sheanse ayns Gaelg
lessons.summary: The science teacher Rhian Tolmie translates a science textbook into Manx for the Manx-medium school, working with the student Tudur: potassium in bananas, fluorine for teeth and iodine in seaweed, the genus that the cat and the lion do not share, the bile made by the liver, the disturbance a stone makes in a lake, a waterfall that grows after rain and the conical shape of a volcano; each hard question about a word is solved in the end.
lessons.text:
Ta Rhian Tolmie ny ynseyder sheanse ayns scoill ayns Doolish raad ta dy chooilley lessoon ayns Gaelg. Agh cha nel lioar sheanse vie ayns Gaelg ec ny paitçhyn. Er-y-fa shen, ta Rhian çhyndaa lioar sheanse veih Baarle gys Gaelg. Ta studeyr aeg, Tudur, gobbraghey marish 'sy tourey.

Ayns y chied rheynn, ta'n lioar loayrt mychione bunstooghyn kemmigagh. Ta enmyn Gaelg ec ram bunstooghyn hannah. Ta potashum ayns bananey, as ta feme ec y corp er potashum. Ta bananey mie son y chorp er-y-fa dy vel potashum ayn. Ta fluoreen ayns stoo son glenney ny feeacklyn, as ta'n fluoreen freayll ny feeacklyn lajer. Ta eeadeen 'sy cheayn, as ta famlagh goaill eeadeen stiagh veih'n ushtey. Ta feme ec y corp er eeadeen neesht.

Ayns y nah rheynn, ta'n lioar loayrt mychione cretooryn. Va feysht doillee ec Rhian: cre'n fockle Gaelg son possan dy horçhyn ta feer cosoylagh rish y cheilley? Hooar Tudur y fockle ayns shenn fockleyr: carroo. Va'n feysht feayslit. “Ta'n kayt as y leion 'sy kynney cheddin,” screeu Rhian, “agh cha nel ad 'sy carroo cheddin. Ta'n kayt ayns un carroo, as ta'n leion ayns carroo elley.”

Ayns y rheynn mychione y corp, ta'n lioar loayrt mychione yn aane. Ta'n aane jannoo buighid. Ta'n buighid buigh ny glass, as t'eh goll veih'n aane dys y collane, raad t'eh brishey sheese yn bee 'sy chorp. Va feysht elley ec Tudur: “Vel buighid ny fockle cooie?” Ren Rhian jeeaghyn ayns ny fockleyryn. Va'n fockle buighid ayns shen, as va'n feysht feayslit reesht.

Eisht ta'n lioar loayrt mychione ushtey. “Tra ta clagh tuittym ayns logh,” ta'n lioar gra, “ta boirrey beg 'syn ushtey. Ta'n boirrey shen skeaylley magh myr tonnyn beggey.” Ta jalloo ayn jeh'n boirrey 'sy logh. Ta jalloo elley ayn jeh eas. Lurg fliaghey trome, ta'n eas thummidagh: smoo yn fliaghey, s'thummidagh yn eas. 'Sy tourey, tra nagh vel fliaghey erbee, cha nel yn eas thummidagh.

Ayns y rheynn s'jerree, ta'n lioar loayrt mychione sleityn. Ta cummey cughlinagh ec volcaan: t'eh lhean ec y bun, as t'eh beg ec y mullagh. Ren Tudur tayrn jalloo jeh volcaan cughlinagh son y lioar.

Ec jerrey y tourey, va'n lioar aarloo. Va dy chooilley feysht feayslit, as hooar ny paitçhyn lioar sheanse noa ayns Gaelg.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta Rhian çhyndaa y lioar sheanse?
Er-y-fa nagh vel lioar sheanse vie ayns Gaelg ec ny paitçhyn.
Cre ta fluoreen jannoo son ny feeacklyn?
Ta'n fluoreen freayll ny feeacklyn lajer.
Kys va'n feysht mychione y fockle carroo feayslit?
Hooar Tudur y fockle carroo ayns shenn fockleyr.
Cre ta'n aane jannoo?
Ta'n aane jannoo buighid.
Cre ta taghyrt tra ta clagh tuittym ayns logh?
Ta boirrey beg 'syn ushtey, as t'eh skeaylley magh myr tonnyn beggey.
Cre'n cummey t'ec volcaan?
Ta cummey cughlinagh ec volcaan.

lessons.title: Lioar shennaghys y phurt
lessons.summary: The local historian Berwyn Rodda writes a book on the history of Douglas harbour with help from his daughter Morfudd: the first steamers and the coal they took on there, the herring and lead the island exported, the cholera, scarcity and hardship of the nineteenth century, the railway carriages that brought visitors to the quay, and the diesel ships of today.
lessons.text:
Ta Berwyn Rodda screeu lioar mychione shennaghys y phurt ayns Doolish. Dagh Jesarn, t'eh goll dys y lioarlann, as t'eh lhaih shenn phabyryn naight. Ta'n inneen echey, Morfudd, goaill jallooyn jeh shenn chaslyssyn son y lioar.

Ayns y chied rheynn, ta Berwyn screeu mychione ny chied lhongyn gaal. 'Sy nuyoo eash jeig, haink y chied gaaltan dys Doolish. Va'n gaaltan shen goll eddyr Doolish as Sostyn, as v'eh ny s'tappee na lhong erbee elley. Lurg tammylt, va ymmodee lhongyn gaal 'sy phurt. Va feme ec dy chooilley gaaltan er geayl, as er-y-fa shen va Doolish ny phurt aalhieeney: va ny lhongyn gaal goaill geayl as ushtey er boayrd ayns shen. Va'n aalhieeney shen obbyr vooar son deiney y phurt.

Ayns y nah rheynn, ta Berwyn screeu mychione assphurtanyn yn ellan. Va skeddan nane jeh ny assphurtanyn smoo: va ny lhongyn goll lesh skeddan dys Sostyn as dys çheeraghyn elley. Va leoaie veih Laksaa ayns ny assphurtanyn neesht.

Agh cha row bea aashagh ec sleih y phurt. Ayns y trass rheynn, ta Berwyn screeu mychione y collyr. Haink y collyr dys Doolish 'sy nuyoo eash jeig, as hooar ymmodee sleih baase. Va'n collyr çheet trooid ushtey nagh row glen. Va genney ushtey glen ayns ny straidyn boghtey, as va genney bee neesht ayns bleeantyn ennagh. Va doccar mooar ec ny lughtyn-thie boghtey: genney argid, genney bee, as çhingys.

“Vel oo screeu mychione y doccar ooilley?” dooyrt Morfudd. “Ta,” dooyrt Berwyn. “Cha nel shennaghys y phurt mychione ny lhongyn ynrican. T'eh mychione y doccar ec ny sleih neesht.”

Ayns y rheynn s'jerree, ta Berwyn screeu mychione ny traenyn. Va carriads traen çheet dys y cheiy lane dy hroailtee veih Sostyn. Va ny troailtee çheet magh ass ny carriadsyn as goll er boayrd y gaaltan. Hooar Morfudd shenn chaslys jeh carriads traen ec y cheiy, as ta'n caslys shen er coodagh y lioar nish.

Jiu, cha nel gaaltan erbee 'sy phurt. Ta ny lhongyn noa goll er deesyl. Ta'n lhong deesyl goll dys Sostyn dagh laa, as cha nel feme eck er geayl. Ec jerrey y lioar, ta Berwyn screeu: “Haink ny lhongyn gaal, as hie ad; hig ny lhongyn deesyl as hed ad. Agh bee'n purt ayn foast.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Berwyn screeu?
T'eh screeu lioar mychione shennaghys y phurt ayns Doolish.
Cre'n fa va Doolish ny phurt aalhieeney?
Er-y-fa dy row ny lhongyn gaal goaill geayl as ushtey er boayrd ayns shen.
Cre va nane jeh ny assphurtanyn smoo?
Va skeddan nane jeh ny assphurtanyn smoo.
Kys va'n collyr çheet?
Va'n collyr çheet trooid ushtey nagh row glen.
Cre hooar Morfudd?
Hooar ee shenn chaslys jeh carriads traen ec y cheiy.
Cre ta ny lhongyn noa goll er?
Ta ny lhongyn noa goll er deesyl.

lessons.title: Lioar coagyraght Saoirse
lessons.summary: Saoirse Feeney, who began with a small café and now runs a restaurant in Peel, writes a cookbook of her grandmother's old recipes while her husband Elfed takes the photographs: bread made with whey, fish seared in a hot pan, berries gathered in a basket, a rare and costly herb that she leaves out, and dishes set on old blue tiles; the book sells well and new guests come to the restaurant.
lessons.text:
Ta oastan beg ec Saoirse Feeney ayns Pheeil, rish y phurt. Roish jeih bleeaney, cha row oastan eck: va thie ooree beg eck, raad va sleih goaill tey as bee beg. Va'n thie ooree feer vie, as lurg tammylt, ren Saoirse oastan jeh. Nish ta sleih çheet dys yn oastan veih dy chooilley ayrn jeh'n ellan.

'Sy gheurey, tra nagh vel ram sleih 'syn oastan, ta Saoirse screeu lioar coagyraght. Ta'n lioar lane dy shenn aghtyn coagyrey veih e shenn-voir. Ta'n sheshey eck, Elfed, goaill ny jallooyn son y lioar.

Ta'n chied aght coagyrey mychione arran meaig. Tra ta sleih jannoo caashey, ta meaig faagit lurg y caashey. Ayns ny shenn laghyn, va sleih jannoo arran lesh y meaig shen. “Ta blayst geyre beg ec arran meaig,” ta Saoirse screeu, “as ta'n blayst shen feer vie lesh eeym as skeddan.”

Ta'n nah aght coagyrey mychione eeast. Ta Saoirse screeu dy lhisagh oo greddey yn eeast ayns aghin feer çheh. “Ny jean greddey yn eeast rish tammylt liauyr,” t'ee screeu. “Greddey eh rish minnid, çhyndaa eh, as greddey eh rish minnid reesht. Eisht ta'n blayst mie foast 'syn eeast.”

'Sy toshiaght y gheurey, hie Saoirse as Elfed dys ny keylljyn lesh bascaid. Hooar ad berrishyn er ny biljyn beggey, as ren ad lhieeney y bascaid lhieu. Ren Elfed goaill jalloo jeh'n bascaid lane dy verrishyn, as ta'n jalloo shen ayns y lioar.

Ayns aght coagyrey elley, va lus tiark. Ta'n lus shoh feer tiark er yn ellan nish, as t'eh feer costal 'sy shapp. “Cha nel mee son cur lus costal ayns y lioar,” dooyrt Saoirse. “Ta'n lioar son sleih cadjin. Cha nel ad son kionnaghey lus tiark as costal.” Er-y-fa shen, ren ee lus elley y reih, nagh vel tiark ny costal.

Son ny jallooyn, ren Elfed soie yn bee er leacanyn gorrym shenn. Va ny leacanyn shen ayns thie shenn-voir Saoirse. Ta daah gorrym ec ny leacanyn, as ta'n bee jeeaghyn aalin orroo.

'Sy vee Averil, haink y lioar magh. Ren ram sleih kionnaghey ee, as haink sleih noa dys yn oastan. Va'n sleih noa briaght son arran meaig as eeast veih'n aghin çheh.

Feyshtyn:
Cre va ec Saoirse roish yn oastan?
Va thie ooree beg eck.
Cre ta meaig?
She meaig y stoo ta faagit lurg da sleih jannoo caashey.
Cre'n blayst t'ec arran meaig?
Ta blayst geyre beg ec arran meaig.
Cre ren Saoirse as Elfed lhieeney lesh berrishyn?
Ren ad lhieeney bascaid lesh berrishyn.
Cre'n fa nagh hug Saoirse y lus tiark ayns y lioar?
Er-y-fa dy vel eh feer costal, as ta'n lioar son sleih cadjin.
Cre'n daah t'ec ny leacanyn?
Ta daah gorrym ec ny leacanyn.

lessons.title: Yn aile 'sy shapp lioaryn
lessons.summary: Gwawr Polwhele, who sells old books in Ramsey, lies awake one night, smells smoke and finds that someone has set fire to a bin by her shop door; the fire service comes quickly, but some books with glossy covers are lost; the forensic officer Gillies Darroch finds a glove, the police find the young man who wore it and he goes before the court, and her neighbours' strength and a few preventive measures help her open again.
lessons.text:
Ta shapp lioaryn shenn ec Gwawr Polwhele ayns Rhumsaa, as t'ee cummal ayns shamyr beg seose staartey. Un oie 'sy gheurey, cha dod ee cadley. Va'n traa jees er y chlag, as v'ee foast dooisht ayns y lhiabbee. Tra v'ee dooisht myr shen, ren ee soar jaagh.

Hie ee sheese staartey dy tappee. Va aile ec dorrys y thie: va peiagh ennagh er chur aile da kishtey ec y dorrys. Ren Gwawr fys y chur er ny fir-aile er y çhellvane, as haink ad ayns minnidyn. Va'n aile ersooyl lurg lieh-oor. “She mie dy row oo dooisht,” dooyrt fer jeh ny fir-aile. “My row oo ny cadley, veagh y shapp ooilley loshtit.”

'Sy voghrey, va Gwawr jeeaghyn er ny lioaryn. Va lioaryn ennagh cailt. Va gloas aalin er coodagh dagh lioar jallooagh, agh va'n gloas shen loshtit ec yn aile, as va ny lioaryn shen cailt. Va lioaryn elley fliugh veih'n ushtey, as va ad cailt neesht.

Haink fer-obbree quaiyllagh: Gillies Darroch. T'eh gobbraghey 'sy sheanse quaiyllagh, as t'eh shirrey cowraghyn lurg aile ny lurg dooinney-varroo. Ren Gillies jeeaghyn er y kishtey loshtit as er y dorrys. “Cha nel ourys erbee orrym,” dooyrt eh. “Ren peiagh ennagh foaddey y kishtey er-y-chooyl. Va'n foaddey jeant lesh pabyr.” Ec yn oirr jeh'n raad, hooar eh lauean doo. Ren eh y lauean y chur ayns poagey veg son y thie quaiyllagh.

Lurg shiaghtin, hooar ny poleenyn dooinney aeg. V'eh er ve giu ram jough yn oie shen, as she lauean echey v'ayn. Hie eh roish y thie quaiyllagh, as dooyrt eh dy row eh feer scuirrit jeh'n foaddey.

Va Gwawr trimshagh, agh haink ny naboonyn eck. Hug ad lioaryn shenn veih nyn dhieyn hene, as ren ad gobbraghey marish 'sy glenney. “Ta lajerid ayns sleih y valley,” dooyrt Gwawr. “Cha nel lajerid aym hene nish, agh ta lajerid ec ny naboonyn aym.”

Hug Gwawr reddyn lhiettalagh er y thie: soilshey mooar ec y dorrys, as greie lhiettalagh ta cur magh sheean ard tra ta jaagh ayn. Dooyrt Gillies dy vel reddyn lhiettalagh myr shen mie, as dy vel ad lhiettal ram aileyn.

Lurg mee, va'n shapp foshlit reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va Gwawr dooisht ec jees er y chlag?
Cha dod ee cadley yn oie shen.
Cre ren peiagh ennagh ec y dorrys?
Ren eh foaddey kishtey ec dorrys y thie.
Cre haghyr da ny lioaryn lesh gloas er y coodagh?
Va'n gloas loshtit ec yn aile, as va ny lioaryn cailt.
Cre hooar Gillies ec oirr y raad?
Hooar eh lauean doo.
Quoi hug lioaryn da Gwawr?
Hug ny naboonyn eck lioaryn shenn veih nyn dhieyn hene.

lessons.title: Claare Nollick ayns Gaelg
lessons.summary: Ailbhe Keane from Ireland makes a Manx-language Christmas programme for television with the children of a Manx primary school: they act the Christmas story around a crib, a small boy plays the drum and they all sing the national anthem; she talks about the renewal of Manx, the steadfastness of the last old speakers, Irish as a treaty language in Europe, and her hope for the language, and the old people of the island watch the programme on their television sets.
lessons.text:
Ta Ailbhe Keane gobbraghey son colught beg ayns Doolish ta jannoo claareyn çhellveeish ayns Gaelg. T'ee veih Nerin, as t'ee loayrt Yernish as Gaelg. 'Sy gheurey shoh, t'ee jannoo claare Nollick marish paitçhyn veih'n Vunscoill.

Ta anaase mooar ec Ailbhe ayns aalaanaghey y Ghaelg. “Roish jeih as daeed blein, cha row agh beggan loayreyderyn ayn,” t'ee gra. “Nish ta paitçhyn gynsaghey ayns Gaelg 'sy Vunscoill, as ta sleih aeg loayrt ee ayns ny shappyn. She aalaanaghey mooar eh.” T'ee gra dy row shassooaght ec ny shenn loayreyderyn: cha daag ad y çhengey, ga dy row sleih elley gra nagh row ymmyd ayn. “Gyn nyn shassooaght, cha beagh aalaanaghey erbee ayn,” t'ee gra.

T'ee loayrt mychione y Yernish neesht. “Roish 2007, va'n Yernish ny çhengey chonaantagh ynrican 'syn Unnaneys Oarpagh,” t'ee gra. “Va ny conaantyn mooarey çhyndaait ayns Yernish, agh cha row docamadyn elley. Va'n staydys conaantagh shen beg, agh va'n Yernish ayns shen.” Ta doghys eck dy bee staydys ec y Ghaelg neesht un laa. “Ta doghys aym,” t'ee gra. “Gyn doghys, cha nel aalaanaghey erbee.”

'Sy chlaare, ta ny paitçhyn cloie skeeal y Nollick. Ta cratçh ayn, jeant jeh fuygh, as ta lhiannoo beg jeant jeh eaddagh ayns y chratçh. Ta ny paitçhyn soie mygeayrt y chratçh, as t'ad goaill arraneyn Nollick ayns Gaelg.

Ta drummey beg ec guilley shey bleeaney d'eash. Ta'n drummey jiarg as buigh. Tra ta ny paitçhyn goaill arrane, ta'n guilley bwoalley y drummey dy meein. Ta sheean y drummey feer aalin 'sy thie mooar.

Ec jerrey y chlaare, ta ny paitçhyn ooilley shassoo, as t'ad goaill yn anthym ashoonagh ayns Gaelg. Ta'n guilley bwoalley y drummey son yn anthym neesht.

Va'n claare er y çhellveeish Laa Nollick. Ayns thieyn ymmodee shenn sleih, va'n çhellveeishan er. Ren ad jeeaghyn er y çhellveeishan, as ren ad clashtyn yn anthym ayns Gaelg. Hooar Ailbhe lettyr veih ben shenn: “Va mee jeeaghyn er y çhellveeishan as va mee keayney. Cha row mee rieau er clashtyn paitçhyn goaill yn anthym ayns Gaelg.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Ailbhe jannoo 'sy gheurey shoh?
T'ee jannoo claare Nollick ayns Gaelg marish paitçhyn veih'n Vunscoill.
Cre va ec ny shenn loayreyderyn, rere Ailbhe?
Va shassooaght oc: cha daag ad y çhengey.
Cre va'n Yernish roish 2007?
Va'n Yernish ny çhengey chonaantagh 'syn Unnaneys.
Cre t'ayns y chratçh?
Ta lhiannoo beg jeant jeh eaddagh ayns y chratçh.
Cre ta ny paitçhyn goaill ec jerrey y chlaare?
T'ad goaill yn anthym ashoonagh ayns Gaelg.
Cre ren ny shenn sleih Laa Nollick?
Ren ad jeeaghyn er y claare er y çhellveeishan.

lessons.title: Lioar y drappeyder
lessons.summary: The climber Iwan Probert is writing a small guidebook for walkers and climbers on a hill in the north of the island, so he walks the route again with his friend Eachann Macaulay: an old farm gateway, a sheep pen, a gravel path with many bends, a stream where they see an eel, a short rock climb with a nylon rope and the cold at the top; in his book he tells readers to bring warm clothes against the cold.
lessons.text:
She drappeyder Iwan Probert. T'eh er ve drappal sleityn as creggyn rish feed blein, ayns Nalbin, ayns Sostyn as ayns Mannin. Nish t'eh screeu lioar veg son sleih ta shooyl as drappal er slieau 'sy twoaie jeh'n ellan. Ayns y lioar, t'eh screeu dagh ayrn jeh'n raad, veih'n toshiaght gys y mullagh.

Un Jesarn 'sy gheurey, hie Iwan seose y slieau reesht marish e charrey Eachann Macaulay, son dy jeeaghyn er y raad son y lioar. Cha nel Eachann ny drappeyder. “Ta mee son shooyl,” dooyrt eh, “agh cha nel mee son drappal creggyn.”

Va toshiaght y raad ec grinney shenn thie eirinagh: grinney jeant jeh clagh, lesh giat yiarn ayn. “Ta'n grinney shoh ny chowrey mie son y lioar,” dooyrt Iwan. “Ta dy chooilley pheiagh fakin y grinney.” Lurg y grinney, va croa son kirree, as va ny kirree 'sy croa. Ren Iwan screeu: “Lurg y grinney, ta croa son kirree er y laue chiare. Dooin y giat, son nagh jean ny kirree roie ersooyl veih'n croa.”

Lurg y croa, va cassan garvel. Ta ram cruillyn ayns y chassan: t'eh goll seose y slieau beggan as beggan. Va'n garvel fliugh lurg y fliaghey. “Jean kiarail er y garvel tra t'eh fliugh,” screeu Iwan. Ren eh coontey ny cruillyn ayns y chassan: va kiare cruillyn jeig ayn. Ec y cruill s'jerree, va strooan beg. Honnick Eachann astan 'syn ushtey: eeast liauyr as thanney, ta snaue fo ny claghyn. “Astan!” dooyrt eh. “Cha row fys aym dy vel astan ayns strooan cho ard.” Hug Iwan yn astan 'sy lioar neesht.

Faggys da'n vullagh, va creg ard. Hug Iwan tead neelane er y chreg. Ta tead neelane eddrym as lajer. Ren Eachann drappal y chreg lesh y tead neelane, as v'eh feer maynrey.

Ec y vullagh, va'n feayght feer trome. Va'n gheay geyre, as va'n feayght ayns nyn laueyn as ayns nyn eddin. Ren ad soie rish minnid ynrican, as eisht hie ad sheese reesht. Ayns y lioar, screeu Iwan: “Ta'n feayght er y vullagh trome, eer 'sy tourey. Gow lhiat eaddagh çheh noi'n feayght.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre ta Iwan screeu?
T'eh screeu lioar veg son sleih ta shooyl as drappal er y slieau.
Vel Eachann ny drappeyder?
Cha nel. T'eh son shooyl, agh cha nel eh son drappal creggyn.
Cre va lurg y grinney?
Va croa son kirree lurg y grinney.
Cre honnick Eachann 'sy strooan?
Honnick eh astan 'syn ushtey.
Cre'n tead hug Iwan er y chreg?
Hug eh tead neelane er y chreg.
Cre lhisagh sleih goaill lhieu noi'n feayght?
Lhisagh ad goaill lhieu eaddagh çheh.
